Photoredox/Copper Dual-Catalyzed Regioselective 1,4-
Arylcyanation of 1,3-Enynes for Multifunctionalized Allenyl Nitriles
Qilong Wu, Xufeng Li, Jian Lv, Yongjia Shi, and Daoshan Yang*
ABSTRACT: A copper/photoredox dual-catalysis-enabled 1,4-arylcyanation of 1,3-enynes to aford tetrasubstituted allenyl nitriles
was initially developed. The reaction features good reaction generality and high reaction regioselectivity, providing facile access to
multifunctionalized allenyl nitriles. This strategy achieves the construction of aryl-containing tetrasubstituted allenyl nitriles via
indirect arene C−H functionalization. It also serves as an important complement to thianthrenium salt chemistry.

In conclusion, we have successfully demonstrated the first
photoredox/copper dual-catalysis-promoted 1,4-arylcyanation
of 1,3-enynes for the synthesis of multifunctionalized allenyl
nitriles using thianthrenium salts as aryl radical precursors. The
reaction features exceptional regio- and chemoselectivities,
mild reaction conditions, and broad functional-group tolerance
and provides an eficient route to the synthesis of aryl-
containing allenyl nitriles in a single step. Mechanistic studies
indicate that aryl thianthrenium salts serve as aryl radical
precursors and will inspire new opportunities for the design of
radical-mediated multicomponent reactions. Further applica-
tions of this method and the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of
optically active allenyl nitriles are currently underway.

photoredox/copper dual-catalysis-promoted 1,4-arylcyanation
of 1,3-enynes for the synthesis of multifunctionalized allenyl
nitriles using thianthrenium salts as aryl radical precursors. The
reaction features exceptional regio- and chemoselectivities,
mild reaction conditions, and broad functional-group tolerance
and provides an eficient route to the synthesis of aryl-
containing allenyl nitriles in a single step. Mechanistic studies
indicate that aryl thianthrenium salts serve as aryl radical
precursors and will inspire new opportunities for the design of
radical-mediated multicomponent reactions. Further applica-
tions of this method and the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of
optically active allenyl nitriles are currently underway.
